verified_by: 3-state differential run by the verification agent's DETERMINISTIC machinery (agent/run_worklist.py over agent/orchestrator.py), Maven, JDK 21, module planetiler-core. First case whose clone, version-knob probe, three states and oracle were driven by the generic runner rather than by a per-repo hand-written acceptance_*.py harness. NOT fully autonomous: SEAM_A (the driver test) was written by Claude in-conversation and passed in with --driver rather than generated by the headless path in agent/seams.py. See agent_provenance.
note: FIRST VERIFIED CASE FOR THE snakeyaml-engine BREAK. The engine entry was added to the catalog on 2026-08-12 from a near-miss (fglock/PerlOnJava) and had no case until now; every earlier snakeyaml case belongs to org.yaml:snakeyaml at the 1.32 boundary.

discovery.discovery_method: GitHub code/commit search for setCodePointLimit, with the library confirmed from the diff (the identifier is spelled identically in org.yaml:snakeyaml and org.snakeyaml:snakeyaml-engine, so the identifier alone cannot tell the two breaks apart).

library._baseline_note: 2.4 is the version planetiler was on immediately before the boundary crossing recorded below, i.e. their own previous version, not a stand-in. It is NOT the version in the tree at the adaptation commit: by September 2024 the POM declared 2.8, so state 1 pairs 2024 code with the 2022 library. An ASSEMBLED baseline, the infoarchive shape rather than the worldedit shape.
library.breaking_boundary: 2.5 (3 MiB / 3145728 code-point ceiling imposed by default)
library.dependency_scope: compile, version managed in the root POM's dependencyManagement, used by planetiler-core

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: direct bump of the managed snakeyaml-engine version in the root POM
in_repo_version_transition._distance_note: The two-year gap is the interesting part, and it is NOT the liquibase pattern the 1.25->1.26 write-up warns about. There the limit never changed for the client and their data merely grew past a ceiling that had always been there. Here the ceiling was IMPOSED by the 2.5 upgrade: before that commit a 4 MB document loaded, after it the same document threw, and the differential below shows exactly that on planetiler's own code. What arrived late was a user with a big schema, not the break.

bump_source: snakeyaml-engine 2.5, which brought the YAML 1.2 engine in line with the DoS hardening snakeyaml 1.32 had applied to the 1.1 parser.

behavioral_break.mechanism: snakeyaml-engine 2.5 caps incoming documents at 3 MiB (3145728 code points) BY DEFAULT and adds LoadSettingsBuilder.setCodePointLimit to raise it. planetiler built its one and only parser as `new Load(LoadSettings.builder().build())` -- default settings -- so the ceiling applied the moment the managed version crossed 2.5, and any schema file over 3 MiB stopped loading.
behavioral_break.observed_exception: org.snakeyaml.engine.v2.exceptions.YamlEngineException: The incoming YAML document exceeds the limit: 3145728 code points.
behavioral_break.blast_radius: Any planetiler user whose custommap schema YAML exceeds 3 MiB. YAML.load is the single entry point for every schema the tool reads, so the break is not confined to one feature.

adaptation.repo_note: planetiler, the OpenStreetMap vector-tile generator. Multi-module Maven; the YAML utility lives in planetiler-core.
adaptation.author: Michael Barry
adaptation.diff:
- private static final Load snakeYaml = new Load(LoadSettings.builder().build());
+ private static final Load snakeYaml = new Load(LoadSettings.builder().setCodePointLimit(Integer.MAX_VALUE).build());
adaptation.shape: RAISE_THE_LIMIT — the default production path is restored for every caller, with no configuration required. Contrast the three knob-exposure adaptations in the sibling 1.32 corpus (swagger-parser, weblogic-deploy-tooling, CommandHelper), where the default stays at 3 MiB and only a caller who sets a property recovers.
adaptation.maintainer_regression_test: The same commit adds planetiler-core/src/test/java/com/onthegomap/planetiler/util/YamlTest.java with testLoadLargeYamlList and testLoadLargeYamlMap, each building a 500 000-entry document. The maintainer's own tests target the ceiling directly, which independently corroborates that this commit is an adaptation to the code-point limit and not an unrelated tidy-up. The driver below was written from the diff before those tests were read, and reproduces the same failure.

verification.method: 3-state differential, one driver source compiled and run unchanged in all three states
verification.driver_summary: Calls planetiler's own YAML.load(String, Map.class) on a single-key document of 4 MiB — the smallest fixture that crosses the ceiling, so nothing else about the parser is under test.

harness_interventions.what: The snakeyaml-engine version was rewritten from the literal <version>2.8</version> in the root POM's dependencyManagement to ${bbc.snakeyaml-engine.version}, and re-applied after every checkout.
harness_interventions.why: planetiler names the version with no property at all, so no -D can move it and the version-knob probe correctly reported that the differential could not be controlled. The rewrite is the same one gen-harness --reuse-pom performs, and it is followed by the probe, which MEASURES that the version now moves before any state runs.
harness_interventions.affects_result: no — applied identically to all three states, and the probe confirms each state ran at the version it claims

harness_interventions.what: Maven ran under agent/settings-bbc.xml, which mirrors Central only.
harness_interventions.why: The user-level ~/.m2/settings.xml carries <mirrorOf>*</mirrorOf>, which also swallows the OSGeo repository planetiler declares for org.geotools. Under it, resolution failed and the probe reported 'build resolved None' — indistinguishable in the ledger from 'this client does not depend on the library'. This candidate would have been discarded as unverifiable for a reason that has nothing to do with the client, the library, or the break.
harness_interventions.affects_result: no — it restores the client's own declared repositories rather than adding anything

harness_interventions.what: bbc/BbcTest.java was written into planetiler-core/src/test/java as an untracked file.
harness_interventions.why: SEAM_A: the driver has to exist somewhere, and untracked means it survives the checkouts between states.
